items.title: Lost Books: Reconstructing the Print World of Pre-Industrial Europe
items.note: Collected volume that set the agenda for counting and recovering lost editions from archival, catalogue and statistical evidence.

items.title: The Legion of the Lost: Recovering the Lost Books of Early Modern Europe
items.note: Argues that whole categories of cheap and ephemeral print are systematically missing from surviving collections.

items.title: The Gutenberg Galaxy's Dark Matter: Lost Incunabula, and Ways to Retrieve Them
items.note: Surveys documentary and fragmentary traces of lost fifteenth-century editions, especially single-sheet and occasional print.

items.title: Lost Incunable Editions: Closing in on an Estimate
items.note: Refines their statistical model of incunable survival, estimating the share of editions surviving in no copy.

items.title: Lost Print in England: Entries in the Stationers' Company Register, 1557–1640
items.note: Matches Stationers' Register entries against surviving copies to measure loss in English print.

items.title: Publicity and Its Uses. Lost Books as Revealed in Newspaper Advertisements in the Seventeenth-Century Dutch Republic
items.who: A. der Weduwen and A. Pettegree
items.note: Uses newspaper book advertisements to identify Dutch editions with no surviving copy.

items.title: Survival Factors of Seventeenth-Century Hand-Press Books Published in the Southern Netherlands
items.note: Shows survival depends strongly on sheet count, binding in Sammelbände and institutional collecting.

items.title: Fifty Thousand Veronicas. Print Runs of Broadsheets in the Fifteenth and Early Sixteenth Centuries
items.note: Documents very large print runs of single-sheet items that now survive in few or no copies.

items.title: Lost Books and Printing in London, 1557–1640
items.note: Monograph-length analysis of lost English editions by genre, finding ballads and cheap religious print most affected.

items.title: The Bookshop of the World: Making and Trading Books in the Dutch Golden Age
items.who: A. Pettegree and A. der Weduwen
items.note: Reconstructs Dutch output from catalogues, advertisements and archives, arguing surviving copies greatly understate production.

items.title: Printing R-Evolution and Society 1450–1500: Fifty Years that Changed Europe
items.note: Results of the ERC 15cBOOKTRADE project, using copy-level provenance data on surviving incunabula to study production and circulation.

items.title: Tracing Lost Editions of Parisian Printers in the Sixteenth Century: The Case of Jean Bonfons and his Widow Catherine Sergent
items.note: Case study of a romance-printing family with low survival, asking how far bibliographies and survival rates distort output.

items.title: Estimating the Loss of Medieval Literature with an Unseen Species Model from Ecodiversity
items.note: First application of ecological richness estimators to the loss of medieval texts.

items.title: copia: bias correction for richness in abundance data
items.note: Python package implementing Chao1 and related unseen-species estimators for cultural datasets, maintained through 2026.

items.title: Book Trade Catalogues in Early Modern Europe
items.who: A. der Weduwen, A. Pettegree and G. Kemp (eds.)
items.note: Essays treating booksellers' and auction catalogues as sources for editions that no longer survive.

items.title: Forgotten books: The application of unseen species models to the survival of culture
items.note: Estimates survival rates of medieval narrative manuscripts and works across six literatures with unseen-species models.

items.title: Demystifying Chao1 with Good-Turing
items.note: Explains the assumptions behind the Chao1 estimator, relevant to judging when such models suit book-survival data.

items.title: The Quaderneto of Padua: A 1480 List of Incunabula for Sale
items.note: Edits a bookseller's list of 1480, a type of document that can reveal editions with no surviving copy.

items.title: On the transmission of texts: written cultures as complex systems
items.who: J.-B. Camps, J. Randon-Furling and U. Godreau
items.note: Models copying and loss as a stochastic process to explain observed stemma shapes and survival; published in PNAS Nexus, June 2026.

items.title: Saved in translation? Diversity shared in French and Dutch medieval literature
items.who: M. Kestemont, F. Karsdorp, J.-B. Camps and R. Sleiderink
items.note: Extends unseen-species estimation to diversity shared between two literatures, using translated works as a test case.
